results.title: OpenVids: Open-source video editor you run by chatting with AI agents | Product Hunt
results.content:
Hi, I made this. OpenVids is a desktop video editor where you describe what you want in chat and agents edit the timeline. A director agent splits the work between specialists (editor, vision, motion design, audio, research), and you watch the timeline change while they work. It's still a normal editor underneath, so you can fix things by hand. It's a fork of HeyGen's HyperFrames. There's no account and no cloud: you bring your own API key and the project is a folder of files on your machine. All your video projects live in one place, instead of being scattered across messy chats in Claude Code or Codex. Two things I built because the first version was bad: - Agents kept saying "done" on videos with black frames or dead audio. results.title: How Loom’s bet on Product Hunt paid off | Product Hunt
results.content:
That decision helped them build a devoted audience in the Product Hunt community. When Loom (then Openvid) launched on Product Hunt in 2016, 3,000 people signed up within the first 24 hours.

Reflecting on their initial launches, Shahed told us, “After talking to users and launching on Product Hunt, we realized the problem was there just wasn't enough brand trust with our product.” So the team focused on engagement, building brand trust, and learning what was inhibiting or propelling their success.

After numerous launches, the team quite literally knew their audience. Instead of just reading comments and silently incorporating feedback, they went a step further.
